Knight.title: Knight
Knight.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Knights are enemies that can normally only be damaged from their exposed brains on the backs of their heads. However, explosions, attacks that pierce enemies (Brimstone, Cupid's Arrow, etc.), or melee attacks (Spirit Sword, Mom's Knife, etc.), will deal damage from any direction. The Knight normally walks around in random directions and will dash at Isaac if he is within line of sight.

sections.heading: Selfless Knight
sections.text: Selfless Knights are considerably faster than regular Knights but otherwise function the same. Rather than an exposed brain, they have Isaac's face on the backs of their heads.

sections.heading: Floating Knight
sections.text: Floating Knights are similar to ordinary Knights but are slightly slower and can fly over obstacles.

sections.heading: Bone Knight
sections.text: Bone Knights are similar to ordinary Knights but leaves behind a short-lasting trail of damaging Red Creep. They charge faster than an ordinary Knight, but not as fast as the Selfless Knight. [Before Repentance] Bone Knights are the only variant of Knights that are susceptible to knockback both from the front and from the back.

sections.heading: Loose Knight
sections.text: Loose Knights are similar to ordinary Knights, but move slower and separates into a Brainless Knight and Pon when killed.

sections.heading: Brainless Knight
sections.text: Brainless Knights are a variant of Knight created when a Loose Knight dies. They alternate between running around the room along the cardinal directions and aimlessly walking in circles, charging at Isaac when he gets in line of sight. It dies when its corresponding Pon dies; otherwise, they are invincible.

sections.heading: Black Knight
sections.text: Black Knights are a variant of Knight that have slightly higher health and will walk erratically around the room, charging at Isaac if he is within line of sight. When charging, they accelerate rapidly, sending waves of fire in the cardinal directions and becoming stunned momentarily after colliding with a wall or obstacle. A Black Knight's mask will also reflect any of Isaac's tears that come in contact with it. They are almost immune to knockback and other forced-movement (such as Black Hole).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] Hagalaz has the following interactions with the Knight and its variations:

• Knight, Floating Knight, Bone Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Brain

• Selfless Knight - Notably, no effect

• Loose Knight, Black Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Pon

• Brainless Knight - Destroys and leaves nothing
[end edition note] 

• The Knight is a monster in two segments: an invisible, invincible "shield" segment that leads the way and the visible "body" that follows close behind. The shield takes no damage and partially covers the body, stopping shots that would damage it.

• Sometimes, when a Knight changes directions, it appears to pause for a moment; this is because the shield segment is moving past the body segment, and the body won't move until the shield moves away from it, the same way the trailing segments of Larry Jr. or Buttlicker chains behave.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Prior to Booster Pack #5, the Knight and its variants were briefly invulnerable when they spawned, or when Isaac entered the room they are in. They would become vulnerable when they started moving.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, Knights were completely vulnerable when they spawned; the shield segment did not cover the Knight's front until it started moving, so Isaac could shoot it in the face for damage as soon as it appeared.

• Items that provide a fear effect (like Dark Matter) work remarkably well because they run away from Isaac, exposing their weak side.

• Items that have a damage-over-time effect (such as Fire Mind or Scorpio) also work well, since hitting them on the shield portion will still inflict the effect and mitigate the need to hit them from behind.

• The name of the monster is a reference to the Darknut (also known as Tartnuc) enemy from The Legend of Zelda who, similar to Knights, cannot be harmed from their front.

• Floating Knights cannot fly over key blocks.

• If Isaac charms a Knight and it is the only enemy in the room, the Knight will chase Isaac but will not charge, making the Knight more difficult to damage until the effect is gone.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Black Knight, Brainless Knight, and Loose Knight first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• In Antibirth, Brainless Knights were referred to as Empty Knights.

• Black Knights had a slightly different appearance in Antibirth and would spawn in the Mausoleum.

• Knights and their variants first appear in Chapter 2 (Caves,Catacombs,Flooded Caves), but become much more common in Chapter 3 (Depths,Necropolis,Dank Depths).

• [Repentance] The functionality of Black Knights and their ability to deflect Isaac's tears from the front is similar to that of Eternal Knight champions in the original flash version of the Binding of Isaac: Eternal Edition.

• [Repentance+] Bone Knight is the only Knight variant that does not play sound effects.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The hitbox of Dark Red Champion Knights (and their variants) do not change when they crumble into goo, and they must be shot from the back to damage them.

Brain.title: Brain
Brain.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Brains slide around the room erratically in the cardinal directions, leaving a trail of red creep, they deal a whole heart of contact damage. When Isaac is within line of sight they will charge in his direction until they collide with an obstacle or another enemy similar to Knights.

sections.heading: Poison Mind
sections.text:
Poison Minds behave like regular Brains, but they slide diagonally and leave a trail of green creep.

[Repentance] Poison Minds float, passing over obstacles, and explode when killed.

sections.heading: Black Globin's Head
sections.text: Black Globin's Heads behave like Brains, but they target Isaac directly, chasing him.

sections.heading: Festering Guts
sections.text: Festering Guts are spawned exclusively by Gutted Fatty. They travel around the room randomly in cardinal directions and occasionally spawn a Charger.

sections.heading: Pon
sections.text:
Pons hop around erratically leaving red creep wherever they land. If close to Isaac then they will hop towards Isaac chasing him similarly to Hoppers.

They can spawn with a paired Brainless Knight in which killing them is required to kill their corresponding Brainless Knight. A Pon and a Brainless Knight pair will always spawn when Loose Knight is killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] If Poison Minds aren't unlocked yet, they are replaced by Brains.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Pon first appeared in the Antibirth mod where it could also appear in Depths.

• [Repentance] The name of Pon is likely a pun in reference to the homophonic pronunciation of the Pons region of the brain and pawns from chess.
